 1             Randomised experiments on networks suffer from interference. A standard estima-

 3             treatment and a summary of neighbours’ treatments, then predicts at all-treated and
 4             all-control. We ask how accurate it is, what determines its error and when it should
 5             not be used, treating it as extrapolation from the exposures the experiment produced
 6             to the two global corners. In simulations with exactly known GATE (six interfer-
 7             ence mechanisms, synthetic and two real graphs, Bernoulli and cluster assignment;

10             model is correct, the standard deviation scales as n−0.50 and (1+d)0.55 in sample
11             size and mean degree. The bias is, on our reading, the response’s curvature times

13             a formula that knows the true response lies inside the 95% Monte Carlo interval
14             of the measured bias in 85% of cells, but how the bias depends on degree differs
15             by mechanism. Regression beats difference-in-means in most cells; the spillover
16             share above which it wins rises with degree, and a threshold mechanism is the
17             exception on synthetic graphs but not on real ones. Two expectations fail: no data-
18             computable score we tried predicts the bias usefully, and nominal 95% intervals

20             on the threshold mechanism three of the five cannot be told apart from it. All
21             outcomes are simulated, and shares describe our grid.


22   1    Introduction
23   Randomised experiments on a social or marketplace network violate the assumption that one unit’s
24   outcome does not depend on another’s assignment, and the quantity of interest is usually the global
25   average treatment effect (GATE): the difference in mean outcome if every unit were treated rather

30   graph-based exposure covariates such as the treated fraction of its neighbours, then predict at the

shown.message:
I approved version 2 (`paper-repo`#10) at head d5cfdfc. I read the system-built `dev` PDF, which is built from a tree identical to that head.

Both `must` findings from the earlier review are fixed:
- **Table 2:** it now has one absolute-R² column per target (log RMSE and log|bias|) and a held-out constant row at −0.24. That matches `results/bias_reference.csv`.
- **Script map:** `REPRODUCE.md` section 9 now has Fig. 9 as the fitted-form oracle and Fig. 10 as the cluster designs, and `CAPTIONS.md` carries the paper's figure numbers.

The `may` items I checked were also answered:
- The abstract and introduction say 85%, which is the figure before the post-hoc finite-n centring.
- The threshold-mechanism learners are described as "cannot be told apart". The wording matches `results/parity_d.csv`, with ratios 0.99, 1.09 and 1.02.
- Appendix C defines each cell population and matches `results/populations.csv`.

The main text still ends on page 9.

Three items remain open for `final`:
- the GNN and cluster Horvitz–Thompson baselines in the paper;
- the P6/P7 confirmatory tests of the corner-interpretation claim;
- legibility of Fig. 1 and Fig. 5C at print size.

I wrote the record to `reviews/v2-paper-pr10-d5cfdfc.md` and noted the approval on issue #2.
